idiom_name: Foundation UndoManager for undo/redo bookkeeping; Operation/OperationQueue for queued commands
implementation_notes: Swift's platform supplies the invoker and the history: UndoManager registers an undo operation per action (registerUndo(withTarget:handler:) takes a closure), keeps the undo and redo groups with levelsOfUndo, canUndo/canRedo and nested grouping, and performs the whole stack in the right order - the documentation even names 'undo the last command run' as a general-purpose use. A command therefore only has to describe its inverse instead of maintaining a history. For deferred or parallel work, Operation/OperationQueue models a command as a one-shot task with dependencies, priority and cancellation, and a Sendable closure is the lightweight form when nothing must be undone.
pitfalls: UndoManager is MainActor-isolated in Swift: registering or performing undo from a background actor is a data race, so undo registration must happen on the same actor that mutates the state.
The registered undo closure captures its target strongly and must be idempotent - registering a compensating undo from inside an undo action is how infinite undo/redo loops start.

Operation objects are single-shot: an executed operation cannot be re-queued for redo, and a concurrent subclass must update isExecuting/isFinished with KVO notifications or the queue will never release it.
